description.purpose: Exchange language-neutral semantic relationship candidates and explicit analysis gaps, bound to exact Git revisions.
description.limitations: Only conservative candidates; schemas and digests cannot establish Git source authenticity, complete dependency closure, build configuration, compiler semantics or runtime behavior.

schema.name: semantic_observations
schema.description: One canonical source-bound observation report per analyzed Git revision.

enum.label: Partial candidates only
enum.description: The producer does not claim complete source dependency coverage.

quality.name: strict_json_schema
quality.description: Each report must validate against semantic-observations.v1.schema.json, including closed object shapes and explicit candidate statuses.

quality.name: receipt_identity
quality.description: Recompute canonical record IDs and report digest, enforce declared counts and uniqueness. This checks consistency, not authenticity.

quality.name: source_replay
quality.description: Independently re-parse pinned Git source blobs and reproduce resolver output before accepting provenance.

team.name: Excession maintainers
team.description: Maintenance responsibility for the public, versioned semantic observation data contract.

context.instructions: Use this dataset only to navigate source-bound semantic import candidates. Before relying on any relationship, independently audit the Git source and language-native resolver. The JSON Schema receipt and ODCS metadata alone do not authenticate source or execution.

verifiedStatements.question: What does CANDIDATE mean in this dataset?
verifiedStatements.answer: A conservative syntax-derived file candidate tied to a pinned Git source. It is not a compiler-confirmed or runtime-observed dependency.

verifiedStatements.question: Does an empty gaps array establish complete coverage?
verifiedStatements.answer: No. Missing observations are not negative evidence, including when no explicit parser gap was reported.

constraints.constraint: Do not use missing edges or empty gaps as permission to skip tests, build validation, or security review.
Do not promote CANDIDATE or UNRESOLVED observations into compiler-verified, runtime-observed, or behaviorally guaranteed relations.
Do not interpret an unkeyed canonical digest or JSON Schema validation as source authentication or an execution attestation.
